meta.title: mont-BidCopilot
meta.description: Dual-mode drafting engine for public procurement work, covering both the tender side (the buyer) and the bid side (the supplier). Registers 21 mont_* tools that the agent can call directly: tender requirement parsing, industry skeleton matching, section drafting, cross-section consistency checks, 18-field tender parsing, score-aligned outlining, section authoring, fact locking, pure-JS .docx export, BM25 knowledge-base search, and a gated workflow engine. Compliance is enforced in code, not in prompts: rules T-B1 to T-B5 refuse to emit clauses that restrict competition by region (local branch office, local performance record, local tax or social-insurance payment site), name a specific brand or supplier, or require a revoked qualification; a hit returns generated=false and no clause text. Fact fields accept only manual entry or a verified company database, so performance records can never be filled from web search or a similar project. Three mandatory gates block export until a human signs off: gate 1 for tender qualification and evaluation criteria, gate 2 for bid-side facts and citations, gate 3 for final compliance review. Gate approval is available only to a human, through the /bidcopilot-gate slash command or a Host-side service; the agent has no approve channel and mont_wf_advance rejects approve, reject, and sign. Every decision appends an audit record carrying the operator, timestamp, SHA-256 of the reviewed content, previous-record hash, and its own sealed hash, so tampering with any record, including the last one, is detectable. Permissions: reads only the enterprise materials directory you point it at, and only when you explicitly name it in a message; writes project folders, section files, and .docx exports under DSH_HOME/bidcopilot/projects; makes no network requests; spawns no processes; reads no credentials; and ships no install-time scripts. It never generates documents in batch for several bidders, never exports while unverified facts remain, and never treats a model output as a verified fact. Turning the plugin off removes all 21 tools and the gate command and stops all file writes; existing project directories stay on disk untouched. Output is always a marked-up draft, not a submission-ready bid, and final legal responsibility rests with the user.
